jobs.title: Environmental Test Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description:
About the role

Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules. Internship is full-time and on-site in San Jose, California.

The Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) team at Muon is responsible for validating spacecraft hardware through unit acceptance testing as well as spacecraft-level integration and environmental testing. As an Environmental Test Engineering Intern, you will support the planning, setup, execution, and analysis of environmental tests used to validate spacecraft hardware against the extreme conditions of launch and space.

You will work alongside experienced environmental test engineers, test engineers, and technicians to prepare hardware and test equipment, develop and execute test procedures, collect and analyze test data, and troubleshoot test issues. This is a hands-on opportunity to gain experience with spacecraft environmental testing and see your work directly contribute to the successful integration and launch of Muon spacecraft.

Muon is a small and fast growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success.

Responsibilities

• Assist environmental test engineers with the planning, preparation, and execution of spacecraft and subsystem environmental testing, including thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, and other qualification or acceptance testing.

• Support test setup and instrumentation, including thermocouples, accelerometers, pressure sensors, and other test measurement equipment.

• Assist with preparing spacecraft hardware, fixtures, ground support equipment, and test configurations for environmental test campaigns.

• Execute functional checkouts and test procedures under engineer supervision before, during, and after environmental testing.

• Monitor test operations and hardware performance, identify anomalies, and support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations.

• Collect, process, and perform preliminary analysis of environmental test data to verify hardware performance and test requirements.

• Support development and improvement of test procedures, test processes, checklists, and laboratory workflows.

• Assist with configuration and operation of environmental test equipment and data acquisition systems.

• Support automation and scripting efforts to improve environmental test setup, monitoring, data collection, and analysis.

• Generate test documentation, data summaries, and reports under the guidance of environmental test engineers.

• Support integration and handling of spacecraft hardware and ground support equipment in cleanroom, laboratory, and environmental test facilities.

• Help maintain a safe, organized, and flight-hardware-ready test environment.

Qualifications

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals, particularly in areas such as mechanics, thermal systems, dynamics, instrumentation, or electrical systems.

• Demonstrated interest in spacecraft environmental testing, laboratory testing, or hardware development.

• Experience with a programming or scripting language for data analysis or test automation, such as Python, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, or C++.

• Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to approach complex technical challenges from a first-principles perspective.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment.

• Ability and willingness to work hands-on with engineering hardware and test equipment.

Nice-to-have Skills

• Previous internship, co-op, research, or laboratory experience involving hardware testing.

• Experience with thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, shock, or other environmental testing.

• Experience with data acquisition systems, instrumentation, sensors, or test equipment.

• Experience developing test procedures, test plans, or test reports.

• Experience with accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, strain gauges, or similar instrumentation.

• Experience with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or other tools used for test automation and data analysis.

• Previous experience on technical project teams such as a CubeSat, rocketry, Formula SAE, Solar Car, or other hardware-focused engineering project.

• Familiarity with spacecraft systems or subsystems and environmental test requirements.

• Experience with hardware integration, troubleshooting, or hardware-in-the-loop testing.

Pay range

Bachelor's students $40/hour

Master's $45/hour

PhD $50/hour

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too.  Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IL, IA, ID, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, VT, VA, WA

This position requires access to export controlled information. To conform to U.S. Government export regulations applicable to that information, applicant must either be (A) a U.S. person, defined as a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (green card holder), (iii) refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, (B) eligible to access the export controlled information without a required export authorization, or (C) eligible and reasonably likely to obtain the required export authorization from the applicable U.S. government agency. jobs.title: Senior Avionics Test Engineer
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As an Avionics Test Engineer, you'll play a key role in the design and operation of critical systems that simulate and stress-test flight hardware to prove it is ready for its trip to space. Your work will be instrumental in ensuring the success of our Winnebago-class spacecraft and future ambitious projects. Your expertise will be crucial in ensuring the vehicle meets its mission objectives, from space manufacturing to hypersonic testing during reentry. This is your opportunity to contribute to technologies that are defining the future of space exploration and make an impact that reaches far beyond the stars.

Responsibilities

• Design, build, and operate test systems for spacecraft avionics components and assemblies to fully exercise components during environmental stress testing and component acceptance testing.

• Develop software in Python to implement and execute test procedures, analyze test data, assess pass/fail criteria, and generate test reports.

• Collaborate with component Responsible Engineers (REs) to identify test cases and develop innovative testing strategies to ensure avionics products meet their intended performance standards across extreme conditions.

• Craft comprehensive test plans for flight hardware, manage and conduct qualification, acceptance, and proto-flight tests.

• Work closely with avionics test systems engineers and manufacturing engineers to standardize test software behavior, user interfaces, and data reporting.

• Contribute to developing engineering best practices, focusing on increased test automation and efficiency.

• Collaborate with avionics systems and flight software engineers to develop and operate Hardware in the Loop (HITL) testbeds to simulate the spacecraft on the ground and ensure all systems are mission-ready.

• Draw from your experiences to help mentor and train new engineers, fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement within the team.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

• At least 5 years of experience in system validation, component testing, or test software development with at least 3 years working on aerospace test systems.

• Proficiency in programming and debugging with Python.

• Experience with electronics test equipment including power supplies, DAQ systems, electronic loads, oscilloscopes and multimeters.

• Familiarity with common sensor types, including thermocouples, RTDs and 4-20mA devices.

• Proficiency with Git source control system.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Prior experience standing up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and driving and operating system-level tests.

• Familiarity with Unix environments.

• Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.

• Experience operating environmental test equipment (vibration shakers, TVAC chambers, or thermal chambers).

• Strong project or program management skills.

• Thrive in a dynamic work environment that values teamwork, innovation, and tackling challenges head-on. Be prepared for exposure to diverse tasks and a commitment to personal and professional growth.

Pay Range

• Salary range: Engineer II: $119,543 - $152,749/per year

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

Benefits

Consider your benefits covered for launch. At Varda, we invest in benefits and perks that support your health, financial well-being, and life beyond work. Benefits vary by position, with packages designed specifically for our regular full-time employees and interns.

Regular Full-Time Positions:

Health & Wellness

• Flexible PTO policy + 12 paid holidays

• 100% company-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plans for employees and dependents with FSA and employer-matched HSA options

• Voluntary accident, hospital, critical illness, and pet insurance

• $120/month wellness reimbursement for gym and fitness expenses

• 12 weeks of parental leave (with supplemental disability leave for CA mothers)

• Family building, pregnancy, parenting and menopause benefits via Maven Clinic

• Sponsored One Medical memberships for employees and their dependents

Financial & Retirement

• Substantial incentive equity in a fully funded space start-up

• 401(k) retirement plan with 6% employer match (immediately vested)

• $20/pay period cell phone reimbursement

• Relocation support for new hires, if needed

Workplace Experience & Perks

• Fully stocked kitchen with lunch provided daily and dinner provided twice weekly

• Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and mission-success celebrations

• Complimentary EV charging

Intern Positions:

Health & Wellness

• Paid observed holidays

• 100% company-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plans for employees and dependents with FSA and employer-matched HSA options

• $120/month wellness reimbursement for gym and fitness expenses

• Sponsored One Medical memberships for employees and their dependents

Financial

• $20/pay period cell phone reimbursement

• Up to $4,000 gross up in relocation support, if eligible

• Up to $850 commute credit through Lyft or car rental reimbursement, if eligible

Workplace Experience & Perks

• Fully stocked kitchen with lunch provided daily and dinner provided twice weekly

• Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and mission-success celebrations

• Complimentary EV charging

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

jobs.title: Senior Associate, Fund Administration (Accounting)
jobs.description:
ABOUT JUNIPER SQUARE

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. We’re the Operations Partner trusted by 2,300+ GPs, unifying technology, data, and fund administration services into a single platform that helps GPs move faster, make better decisions, and scale with precision. With $300B+ under administration and 700,000+ LPs on platform, we’ve built the scale to match our ambition. And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

Our culture is built for people who want to do ambitious, meaningful work alongside exceptionally talented teammates. We think like owners, move with urgency, and take pride in solving hard problems that truly matter to our customers and the future of private markets. We believe the best ideas come from open debate, deep collaboration, and diverse perspectives, which is why we believe transparency is the default and feedback makes us stronger. If you’re energized by high standards, rapid growth, and the opportunity to help define a category at a pivotal moment, come join us!

Juniper Square offers employees a variety of ways to work, ranging from a fully remote experience to working full-time in one of our physical offices. We invest heavily in digital-first https://blog.junipersquare.com/juniper-square-ponders-future-of-office-with-digital-first-hybrid-workplace-strategy/ operations, allowing our teams to collaborate effectively across 27 U.S. states, 2 Canadian Provinces, India, Luxembourg, and England. We also have physical offices in San Francisco, New York City, Mumbai and Bangalore for employees who prefer to work in an office some or all of the time.




ABOUT YOUR ROLE

We are hiring a few Senior Associates to join our team. This is an exciting opportunity to join a fast paced start-up environment to help build out Juniper Square’s Fund Administration service offering. Juniper Square is on a mission to transform the Fund Administration offering to Private Markets. We are more than a Fund Administrator, we are a Modern Fund Administrator.  As a Senior Fund Accountant you will partner with the customer, other members of the fund accounting team, and Investor Services and Fund Administration Onboarding teams to deliver  fund accounting and reporting services to Juniper Square’s Private Market customers in the Real Estate, Private Equity, and Venture Capital space. You will have a significant opportunity to shape the trajectory of our service offering and in so doing help to deliver a best-in-class experience to our customers. We are a team of values based self-starters with a curious mindset and the motivation to use technology to our advantage so that we are continually iterating and improving on the status quo. This is an opportunity to couple prior education and experience and to learn from some of the best talent in Private Markets.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Support  major decisions regarding team buildout and operational policies and procedures

 - Define and support the implementation of fund administration workflows, applying best practices and process efficiencies

 - Interface directly with clients to deliver an outstanding client experience

 - Serve as a technical accounting expert and key advisor on significant business/accounting decisions for the team

 - Perform accounting, analytical, & financial reporting duties; ensure client and investor reporting is prepared and completed timely and accurately

 - Review waterfall calculations and capital calls and distributions in accordance with clients’ Limited Partnership Agreements

 - Prepare and review asset- and fund-level performance metrics (IRRs, TVPI, etc.)

 - Assist in preparing, compiling, and verifying external client and regulatory reporting

 - Prepare financial information for stockholders/investor reports

 - Assist with annual audits, including preparation of the initial draft of the annual audit report and related schedules and disclosures; assist with PBC list (Prepared By Client) and tax returns

 - Research and assist in interpreting the impact of recent accounting developments




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of fund accounting or audit experience with exposure to Private Equity, Venture Capital, Private Credit and/or Real Estate funds

 - Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or related field required. 

 - Investran experience preferred.

 - Exposure to complex fund structures, waterfall calculations, performance metrics (IRRs), distributions and capital calls calculations

 - Experience with annual reporting (audited financial statements) 

 - Passion for technology and a desire to use technology to improve business operations

 - Experience scoping out system requirements and implementing new systems

 - Strategic thinker with the ability to master both the details and the big picture

 - Ability to handle many projects at once without losing track of the details

 - Comfortable with ambiguity, excellent work ethic and likes to take ownership of your work


At Juniper Square, we believe building a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture makes us a better company. If you think this job sounds like a fit, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the qualifications.




COMPENSATION 

Compensation for this position includes a base salary, equity, and a variety of benefits. The U.S. base salary range for this role is $85,000 - $98,000. The Canadian base salary range for this role is $80,000 - $100,000. Actual base salaries will be based on candidate-specific factors, including experience, skillset, and location, and local minimum pay requirements as applicable. We are actively hiring for this role in Canada, and offer competitive local pay and benefits. Your recruiter can provide further details.



Benefits include:

 - Health, dental, and vision care for you and your family

 - Life insurance and disability coverage

 - Mental wellness coverage

 - Fertility and growing family support

 - Flex Time Off in addition to company-paid holidays

 - Paid family leave, medical leave, and bereavement leave policies

 - 401k retirement savings plan

 - Healthcare FSA and commuter benefits programs

 - Allowance to customize your work and technology setup at home

 - Annual professional development stipend

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As an RF Component Engineer at Varda, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring seamless connectivity between our satellite vehicles and ground stations. You will be responsible for the complete lifecycle of each RF component, collaborating closely with RF Systems Engineers to define component specifications and to either select or design the necessary hardware. Your work will be crucial in rigorously validating components before their deployment to space. This role requires a strong sense of ownership over your hardware, continually setting new standards for testing RF components before flight.

Some people say that you only have one chance to fly to space so you must be certain it will work. At Varda, we believe that the trip to space and back is the easiest trip our hardware takes. We stress our components above and beyond the levels it should expect to see in flight and we investigate our failures thoroughly. Come join our team and build quality electronics that you will get to see fly over and over again.

Responsibilities

• Serve as the Responsible Engineer for RF flight components, including radios, power amplifiers, antennas and filters.

• Collaborate with RF Systems Engineers to refine product specifications, select or design appropriate components, and oversee the entire product lifecycle.

• Work closely with Flight Software, Structures, and Integration & Test teams to document cross-functional interface requirements for a successful deployment of hardware onto the flight vehicle.

• Take ultimate ownership of product acceptance and qualification testing for space environments, including Thermal, Vibration, Shock, TVAC, and EMI.

• Develop test software to automate equipment, stimulate, and measure component performance, ensuring consistent flight hardware readiness.

• Conduct root cause analysis on test failures and implement comprehensive mitigation strategies for flight risks.

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. in Electrical Engineering, RF Engineering, or a related field. Open to candidates of all experience levels, with role and responsibility adjustments made accordingly.

• Strong hands-on experience with RF test equipment including VNAs, spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, function generators, power meters and power supplies.

• Familiarity with RF components including LNAs, power amplifiers, mixers, filters, oscillators/synthesizers, attenuators, and switches.

• Experience designing and integrating RF components into complete transmit or receive signal chains.

• Proven track record of extreme ownership over projects, leading them to successful completion.

• Proficiency with Python, familiarity with test software libraries like PyVISA for communication with test equipment.

• Demonstrated curiosity and commitment to exploring foundational concepts and pursuing detailed insights with diligence.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Prior experience standing up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and driving and operating system-level tests.

• Familiarity with Unix environments.

• Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.

• Experience operating environmental test equipment (vibration shakers, TVAC chambers, or thermal chambers).

• Strong project or program management skills.

• Thrive in a dynamic work environment that values teamwork, innovation, and tackling challenges head-on. Be prepared for exposure to diverse tasks and a commitment to personal and professional growth.

Pay Range

• Salary range: Engineer II: $144,020 - $184,026/per year

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
Brain Corp is a San Diego, California, USA-based AI company creating transformative core technology for the robotics industry. Our purpose is to create autonomous technology that helps the real world work better. Brain's robotic and AI solutions help retailers ensure that the right product is on the right shelf at the right price, in a clean environment. Through the BrainOS® Robotics Platform, which powers the largest global fleet of the Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) in operation in commercial public spaces, Brain Corp delivers insightful and efficient automated solutions in both commercial floor cleaning and inventory management, empowering organizations and their employees to achieve more. Brain Corp currently powers more than 30,000 AMRs, representing the largest fleet of its kind in the world. Brain Corp is funded by the SoftBank Vision Fund, Clearbridge, and Qualcomm Ventures.

Named a top workplace by the San Diego Union Tribune and USA today in 2025, we make life-changing impacts through innovation, helping workers globally unlock their abilities in orchestration with intelligent machines.

Position Overview:

As a Senior Product Manager, you will identify market problems, use cases, and outcomes for our AI and autonomy platform, BrainOS®, and associated product lines.

Brain Corp is a customer-driven company, meaning you will engage directly with end-users and manufacturers to understand their problems and define opportunities. You will partner closely with engineering, program management, and other stakeholders to increase customer delight, drive sales, and deliver the right business outcomes. This role sits within a dedicated team of professionals operating in a fast-paced, collaborative, start-up-like environment.

The ideal candidate is excited about developing bleeding-edge technology for an emerging market, is business-oriented, and is driven to ensure Brain Corp remains a market leader in the autonomy space

Essential Job Functions:

Roadmaps and Strategy

• Lead Brain Corp’s product vision and strategy for the designated product area while addressing customer needs and aligning with other business objectives

• Develop and manage a roadmap to increase customer satisfaction, meet key milestones, and achieve business objectives

• Influence key business objectives by driving product vision

Customer and Partner Engagement

• Engage directly with our customers (adopters, end-users, and manufacturers) to gather user feedback, understand problems, and define opportunities

• Work directly with US and international channel partners’ technical and business teams to launch and support Brain Corp technology

• Influence customer management, sales, and marketing initiatives

• Conduct product demos and present confidently to potential customers

• Establish clear communication channels with customers and partners

• Act as the primary liaison and main point of contact with program leadership from partner organizations for product-related areas

Research and Discovery

• Build quantitative and qualitative use cases to drive new products, features, and service proposals

• Lead market analysis initiatives and build market expansion plans

• Discover the necessary data to focus and clarify “the what and the why”

• Define pricing and feature tiers

Execution

• Collaborate with and influence program management, design, engineering, sales**,** and market-facing teams

• Direct proof-of-concept prototypes and user tests

• Develop, align, and meet the expectations of strategic programs

• Other duties and projects as assigned

• Other duties and projects as assigned

Education and/or Work Experience Requirements:

• 4-8 years of hands-on product management or product development experience

• Prior experience building, launching, and managing successful B2B products

• Advanced knowledge of product management principles

• Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams (sales, marketing, product development, operations) is essential

Required Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Other Characteristics:

• Thrives in ambiguity and brings order to chaotic, fast-moving startup environments

• Compelling storyteller with outstanding presentation and communication skills

• Demonstrated leadership abilities and stakeholder management

• A gritty problem-solver who thrives on wearing multiple hats, rolling up their sleeves, and executing in the details

• Analytical and data-driven in all decision-making

• Habitually questions the status quo

• Focused on customer-centricity in all decisions and outcomes

• Enthusiastic, positive, and adaptable

• Ability to travel to domestic and international sites regularly (30% travel)

Things That Make a Difference:

• Experience in retail operations strategy, customer experience, retail technology, business continuity, brand governance, and continuous improvement and innovation

• Experience with retail merchandising operations and optimization strategies, including pricing and promotions, planning and execution, costs and deals, category management, and competitive planning

• Experience in omnichannel merchandising processes and systems

• Previous responsibility for significant market share and brand growth at scale is highly desired

• Strong technical capability across both software and hardware

• Understands and embraces disruption, both internally and externally

• Startup or rapid-growth-stage technology company experience is highly desirable

• Highly collaborative and team-oriented

• Solid project management skills

• Keen interest in new technologies

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Essential functions may require maintaining the physical condition necessary for sitting, walking or standing for periods of time; operating a computer and keyboard; use of hands to finger and grasp; talk and hear at normal room levels; visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, and thoroughness of the work assigned or to make general observations of facilities or structures; push or pull up to 50 pounds.

The noise level in the work environment is usually quiet to moderate. Employees are exposed to the typical office environment with computers, printers and telephones.

The installation, setup and testing of our product occur during business off-hours. Therefore, when traveling to customer sites the employee can expect to work either late in the evening (9 p.m. to 2 a.m.) or early in the morning (3 to 8 a.m.).

jobs.title: Industrial Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.description:
About the role

Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules. Internship is full-time and on-site in San Jose, California.

The Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) team at Muon is responsible for the assembly, integration, and validation of spacecraft hardware through unit acceptance testing as well as spacecraft-level integration and testing. As an Industrial Engineering Intern, you will support the development and improvement of the processes, tools, and systems that enable Muon to efficiently build and test spacecraft at scale.

You will work closely with AIT, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Test Engineering teams to analyze production data, improve workflows, identify bottlenecks, develop capacity models, and implement process improvements. This is a hands-on opportunity to apply industrial engineering principles in a fast-growing spacecraft manufacturing environment and directly contribute to increasing production efficiency and throughput.

Muon is a small and fast growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success.

Responsibilities

• Analyze spacecraft assembly, integration, and test processes to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, quality, throughput, and scalability.

• Develop and maintain process maps, standard work, work instructions, and other manufacturing documentation.

• Collect and analyze production data to identify trends, bottlenecks, constraints, and opportunities for improvement.

• Support development of production capacity and resource planning models for spacecraft assembly and test operations.

• Assist with production scheduling, workflow optimization, and resource allocation across AIT operations.

• Conduct time studies and process observations to establish baseline cycle times, labor requirements, and process performance.

• Support development and implementation of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Identify opportunities to improve material flow, kitting, tooling, workstation layout, and overall factory/lab utilization.

• Develop dashboards, reports, and other data-driven tools to provide visibility into production performance and operational metrics.

• Support root-cause investigations and corrective actions for production constraints, process inefficiencies, and recurring issues.

• Partner with technicians and engineers to identify practical improvements to spacecraft assembly and test processes.

• Support implementation and validation of process improvements on the production floor.

• Assist with developing scalable processes and systems to support increasing spacecraft production volume.

• Document process improvements and communicate findings and recommendations to cross-functional stakeholders.

Qualifications

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, or a related technical field.

• Strong understanding of engineering, manufacturing, and/or operations fundamentals.

• Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to use data to identify process improvements.

• Experience with Excel or similar tools for data analysis, modeling, and visualization.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment.

• Ability to work hands-on in a production, laboratory, or engineering environment.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Ability to approach complex operational challenges from a first-principles perspective.

Nice-to-have Skills

• Previous internship, co-op, research, or project experience in industrial engineering, manufacturing, operations, or production environments.

• Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, value-stream mapping, or other continuous improvement methodologies.

• Experience conducting time studies, capacity analysis, line balancing, or process optimization.

• Experience with production planning, scheduling, or resource capacity modeling.

• Experience with data visualization or analytics tools such as Python, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, or similar.

• Experience with CAD or facility/workstation layout tools.

• Experience developing automated spreadsheets, dashboards, or other operational tools.

• Previous experience on technical project teams such as a CubeSat, rocketry, Formula SAE, Solar Car, or other hardware-focused engineering project.

• Familiarity with manufacturing, assembly, integration, or test processes for complex electromechanical hardware.

• Experience working in a cleanroom, laboratory, or aerospace manufacturing environment.

Pay range

Bachelor's students $40/hour

Master's $45/hour

PhD $50/hour

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too.  Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IL, IA, ID, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, VT, VA, WA

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations applicable to that information, applicant must either be (A) a U.S. person, defined as a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (green card holder), (iii) refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, (B) eligible to access the export controlled information without a required export authorization, or (C) eligible and reasonably likely to obtain the required export authorization from the applicable U.S. government agency. jobs.title: Senior Accountant, e-Commerce (Contract)
jobs.description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Senior Accountant – E-Commerce Accounting

Inventory • COGS • Sales • Cash Application • SAP & System Integrations

Position Summary
The consultant will support full-cycle accounting for the online store, from customer orders and inventory movement through revenue, cost of goods sold, accounts receivable, cash application, refunds, and financial reporting. This role will partner with Accounting, Operations, E-commerce, Supply Chain, and IT to resolve reconciliation and system-integration issues involving e-commerce, order management, inventory, payment, and SAP platforms.

Key Responsibilities

·       Own full-cycle accounting for online store activity, including inventory, sales, cost of goods sold, accounts receivable, cash, refunds, credits, and related balance sheet accounts.

·       Perform monthly and quarterly close activities, including journal entries, account reconciliations, variance analysis, and review of transaction completeness and accuracy.

·       Reconcile inventory subledger activity to SAP, including receipts, transfers, adjustments, returns, write-offs, and inventory reserves where applicable.

·       Review and reconcile cost of goods sold to product sales and inventory movement, investigating unusual margins, timing differences, and data issues.

·       Support the complete order-to-cash cycle, including sales orders, fulfillment, billing, revenue recognition, customer receivables, refunds, credits, and cash application.

·       Reconcile payment processor and bank activity to customer orders, accounts receivable, and SAP postings; research unmatched or failed transactions.

·       Partner with Operations, E-commerce, Supply Chain, IT, and Finance teams to understand transaction flows across multiple systems and ensure accurate accounting in SAP.

·       Investigate integration issues between sales, order management, inventory/warehouse, payment, and SAP systems, and determine the accounting impact of incomplete, duplicated, delayed, or incorrect transactions.

·       Participate in system implementations, integration changes, user acceptance testing, and validation of automated accounting entries and interfaces.

·       Develop and maintain reconciliation tools and controls to confirm that data transferred between operational systems and SAP is complete and accurate.

·       Identify root causes of accounting and system issues, coordinate resolution with technical and operational teams, and help prevent recurring problems.

·       Create and maintain process documentation, system flow documentation, and internal controls for online store accounting processes.

·       Identify opportunities to simplify, automate, and strengthen accounting processes as online store activity and systems evolve.

Qualifications

·       Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.

·       Approximately 2–6 years of accounting experience, preferably including inventory, revenue, order-to-cash, e-commerce, retail, or consumer product accounting.

·       Strong understanding of general ledger accounting, reconciliations, month-end close, inventory accounting, revenue, accounts receivable, and cash.

·       Experience with SAP strongly preferred; experience with other large ERP systems is also valuable.

·       Experience working with e-commerce platforms, order management systems, warehouse/inventory systems, payment processors, or system integrations is a plus.

·       Strong Excel and data analysis skills, with the ability to work through large transaction populations and identify exceptions.

·       Ability to understand end-to-end transaction flows and translate operational or system issues into accounting impacts.

·       Strong problem-solving, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

jobs.title: Senior Finance Manager, Product & Engineering
jobs.description:
About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com.

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Finance Manager to serve as a key partner to Mixpanel’s Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD) organizations. This person will own infrastructure cost, EPD opex, and headcount planning while building scalable systems to improve visibility and decision-making, as well as the analytical frameworks that guide how Mixpanel deploys capital and allocates resources across these areas. You’ll partner cross-functionally with Engineering and Product leadership, People, and Finance to ensure investments are intentional, efficient, and aligned with long-term company strategy.

Responsibilities

• Own the Product investment envelope – Manage OpEx and headcount budgets across EPD. Ensure investments align with company strategy while maintaining efficient spend and margin targets.

• Drive rigorous workforce planning across technical and corporate teams – Build bottoms-up headcount models by function and level. Partner with Engineering leaders to sequence hiring against roadmap needs, compliance requirements, and operational scale.

• Model infrastructure and internal systems economics – Develop clear forecasting models for cloud hosting, AI/compute, internal tooling, SaaS applications, and enterprise systems. Identify optimization opportunities across both product infrastructure and corporate tech stack.

jobs.title: Director, NA Sales & Business Development, Running
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Director of NA Sale & Business Development - Running is accountable for leading, developing, and executing a strategic go-to-market plan within running specialty and all other channels to establish KEEN as a credible and emerging running brand. This role is critical in supporting the VP of Sales to cultivate strong customer relationships, collaborating with internal cross-functional and elevating KEENs assortment with the right retail partners to deliver impactful results. This role plays an integral part in pioneering our industry leading outdoor brand in running with the US Marketplace.

Description

• Partners with Sales, Marketing, and Product teams to advance KEEN’s performance categories by developing engagement strategies for run specialty, outdoor specialty, and other strategic retail partners. Builds brand awareness and supports growth in Trail and KEEN Run.

• Cultivates new relationships and strengthens existing customer partnerships within the running specialty category. Focuses on expanding wholesale distribution and building the dealer network in run specialty to scale KEEN’s presence and assortment breadth.

• Identifies and evaluates new account opportunities within run specialty, focusing on key, influential, and credible retail partners to expand the brand’s presence and drive sales growth.

• Assists in developing and executing the go-to-market strategy for KEEN Run, ensuring alignment with product initiatives and the overarching brand vision across all distribution channels.

• Conducts product demonstrations that showcase performance technologies and equip retailers with knowledge of key selling features and benefits. Provides education that supports retailer success and omnichannel product promotion.

• Collaborates with network dealers to analyze performance and drive sales growth, business development, and increased market share for the brand.

• Conducts performance analyses and provides leadership with business insights that inform revenue-growth initiatives and strategic planning. Evaluates the North American running specialty market to identify and recommend growth opportunities.

• Prepares and delivers comprehensive business reports for leadership and stakeholders, including sell-in and sell-through performance, competitive analysis, product demand and availability, and market-share insights.

• Collaborates with internal Marketing and Merchandising teams to develop and execute sell-through and activation strategies tailored to the run specialty channel.

• Leverages data, performance metrics, and brand trends to guide decision- making and develop strategies for future growth opportunities.

• Helps achieve and exceed KEEN Run sales targets by partnering with Marketing, Product, Operations, and Training to deliver results.

Please note this job description is not designed to contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without cause.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's Degree in Business, Marketing, Management, or related field required.

• Eight (8) years experience in sales, specialty account management or related field. Experience in outdoor and run footwear or retail.

• Three (3) years leading and managing a team.

Any equivalent combination of experience and education which clearly indicates the ability to perform the essential functions of the position may substitute on a year for year basis.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

• Deep understanding of the trail running market, including consumer trends, key accounts, and competitor landscapes.

• Familiarity with retail environments, omni-channel strategies, and direct-to-consumer sales models. Expertise in running and or outdoor specialty account base.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and drive strategic decisions.

• Exceptional communication, presentation, and negotiation skills to engage with key accounts and stakeholders.

• Proven ability to develop and execute GTM (go-to-market) strategies and lead product positioning efforts.

• Demonstrated ability to build strong, collaborative relationships with both internal teams and external partners.

• Proficiency with sales analytics tools (e.g., Salesforce, Power BI) and Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).

• Ability to analyze and interpret sell-through data and market trends to identify growth opportunities.

Travel Required: Yes, up to 50% of the time

Why Work at KEEN:  Driven by a passion for life outside, KEEN is a values-led, independently owned brand from Portland, Oregon, that’s on a mission to create original and versatile products, improve lives, and inspire outside adventure. Founded in 2003, KEEN launched a revolution in the footwear industry with the introduction of the Newport adventure sandal and has donated more than $18 million to non-profit organizations and causes around the world to promote responsible outdoor recreation, including conservation efforts to protect open spaces. jobs.description:

The successful candidate will combine workplace strategy, design leadership, and project delivery expertise to drive workplace transformation projects from concept development through implementation.

SR AI ENGINEER, PLATFORM INFRASTRUCTURE, SPECIAL PROGRAMS

• Design and build the deployment generator.

• Create and maintain platform documentation.

• Build the bundle pipeline.

• Implement profile-driven rendering for public cloud, enterprise on-prem, and classified air-gap targets based on profile selection.

• Build and maintain the cross-profile CI matrix.

• Build the testing and validation framework.

• Integrate with the existing Supercompute team's operators, Helm charts, and CRDs by consuming their work as inputs to the generator without modifying production infrastructure.

• Own the monitoring stack migration.

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, mathematics, computer engineering, physics, data science, or engineering discipline.

• 5+ years of experience in Go Lang and/or Python.

• 5+ years of experience working with Kubernetes or similar tooling for automating, developing and scaling containerized applications.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret or Top Secret SCI clearance.

• Experience building CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation (Buildkite, GitHub Actions, or equivalent).

jobs.title: Senior Paralegal, Marketing
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary:

At The Coca‑Cola Company, every marketing touchpoint matters—because every interaction reflects our commitment to trust, compliance, and consumer confidence. Our Marketing Legal team ensures that consumer-facing communications drive growth within the guardrails of ethical, responsible, and legally sound practices.

As a Senior Paralegal, you will play a critical role in supporting the North America Operating Unit (NAOU) Marketing Function. You’ll review a wide spectrum of advertising and promotional materials, identify and escalate regulatory risks, and enable speed-to-market while maintaining compliance with FTC, FDA, and consumer protection regulations. This position blends deep subject matter expertise with a business-oriented approach, operating under attorney supervision in a fast-paced, high-volume environment where agility and precision are essential.

If you are energized by marketing innovation, meticulous about legal and regulatory detail, and passionate about helping brands connect responsibly with consumers across evolving channels and platforms, this role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact at scale

Key Responsibilities

Provide supervised legal and business advice to cross-functional business partners regarding day-to-day marketing legal matters, including promotions and sponsorships, advertising claims, third-party intellectual property rights, digital and social media campaigns, influencer and content creator best practices, basic privacy guardrails (including the collection and use of identifiable consumer data), and emerging issues related to the use of AI in marketing.

• Review and approve all types of marketing materials across all media channels — including digital, social media, broadcast, print, out-of-home, point-of-sale, packaging, and emerging platforms — for compliance with applicable federal, state, and local advertising and consumer protection laws, FTC Act guidelines, FDA regulations, and third-party intellectual property rights.
• Identify advertising and marketing claims, including health, wellness, nutritional, and comparative claims.
• Support the legal team's compliance initiatives by identifying potential legal and regulatory risks in marketing campaigns and proactively escalating issues to attorneys as appropriate.
• Manage the day-to-day legal review process within the company's review and approval platform ensuring marketing materials proceed efficiently through the approval workflow while maintaining thorough documentation of legal review.
• Assist the business in the development, drafting, review, and negotiation of contracts that reflect agreed-upon business terms, including but not limited to sponsorship agreements, promotional agreements, influencer, talent agreements.
• Leverage AI tools and legal technology platforms to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of legal review workflows, marketing compliance processes, and research tasks.
• Participate in additional cross-functional projects and initiatives as assigned by the legal team.

Position Details:

Location: Atlanta, GA

Role Type: Individual Contributor (No Direct Reports)

Work Model: Hybrid – 3 days onsite, 2 days virtual

Required Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree or Associate's degree in Paralegal Studies from an ABA-accredited program, or a Bachelor's degree in a related field with a paralegal certificate from an ABA-accredited program.

Experience & Skills

• 5+ years of experience as a transactional paralegal, with significant experience in advertising, marketing, and/or consumer products law.
• Experience in an in-house legal team, preferably within a large consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, or similarly situated company, with the ability to translate legal requirements into practical, scalable guidance for legal and non-legal stakeholders.
• Demonstrated experience with federal, state, and local consumer protection laws and FDA regulations as they relate to advertising and marketing compliance.
• Experience using AI-assisted tools to enhance and simplify legal work in a legal or marketing compliance environment, including reviewing materials, conducting research, issue identification, and managing and designing workflows and identifying opportunities to automate routine marketing legal workflows, while validating AI-generated outputs for accuracy, completeness, consistency with approved legal guidance.
• Maintains high-quality information and can use basic reporting and analytics to identify trends, workload patterns and opportunities for improvement.
• Experience using a review and approval platform for marketing materials including managing review workflows, documenting approvals, and maintaining compliance records within the system.
• Demonstrated ability to identify advertising and marketing claims — including health, nutritional, wellness, environmental, comparative, ingredient, and performance claims.
• Proven ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment with continuously evolving demands and competing priorities, demonstrating strong organizational skills, sound judgment, and the ability to adjust priorities in response to unanticipated events.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Outlook, Teams, Excel, PowerPoint, and SharePoint.
• Comfortable learning and using emerging legal technology, workflow automation and AI tools; understands their capabilities and limitations and can appropriately validate technology-assisted work.
• Exceptional attention to detail, ensuring that all necessary steps are taken to perform tasks in a safe, effective, and quality manner.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex legal concepts clearly and concisely to non-legal business partners.
• Flexibility and adaptability in dealing with changing situations, evolving business needs, and diverse stakeholders across the Marketing Function.
• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a cross-functional team environment, exercising initiative and sound judgment under attorney supervision.

What We Can Do for You

Commitment to Diversity: We are paving the way to create change in the industry, and our leadership is committed to diversity, inclusion, and belonging.

Global Network: Expand your global network by developing, learning, and growing with our top talent and connections around the world.

Agile Work Environment: We embrace agility, with leadership that believes in removing barriers so you are empowered to innovate and discover new solutions to complex problems.

Accordingly, all applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require The Coca-Cola Company's sponsorship to continue to work legally in the United States.

jobs.title: Government Affairs Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
Your Impact
The Government Affairs Operations Analyst provides integrated policy research, operational, logistical and administrative support to advance Lowe's public policy and government relations priorities. This role monitors and evaluates legislative, regulatory, and administrative developments; prepares clear, actionable analyses; and maintains accurate records and compliance documentation. This position also supports the efficient operation of the Washington, DC office and government affairs team through scheduling, budget tracking, invoice and expense processing, travel and event coordination, and executive support. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, discreet, and able to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment with senior leaders and external stakeholders.

What You Will Do

• Analyze government affairs activities, campaigns, and stakeholder engagement efforts and provide support for compliance analysis, administration, and applicable federal, state, and local reporting requirements.
• Gather intelligence and support preparation of legislative testimony, policy positions, executive briefings, and presentations related to pending or emerging legislative and regulatory matters.
• Develop project plans, timelines, run-of-show documents, and other planning materials to coordinate internal teams, external vendors, and business partners through program and event execution.
• Monitor, analyze, and report on legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments impacting Lowe’s; identify emerging trends and issues and support development of position papers, policy briefings, presentations, and other materials for business and government affairs leadership.
• Coordinate with vendors and service providers, including sourcing support, pricing discussions, deliverables, timelines, and contract-related activities in partnership with procurement, legal, and finance.
• Serve as a key point of contact for Washington, DC office operations and contribute to special projects and process improvements that strengthen the effectiveness of the government affairs team.
• Support the planning and execution of government affairs meetings, fly-ins, conferences, receptions, stakeholder engagements, and other events, including logistics, communications, briefing materials, registration, and onsite coordination.
• Track the government affairs budget and program-related expenses; process invoices, purchase orders, sponsorships, and vendor payments; and partner with finance to reconcile spending and support forecasting.
• Support government affairs leadership and senior executives with briefing materials, schedules, travel, meeting preparation, stakeholder information, and event logistics.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in political science, public policy, law, government, business administration, communications, or a related field or equivalent years of experience in lieu of education requirement, if applicable
• 3 years of experience in government affairs, legal research, public policy, regulatory affairs, corporate affairs, administrative operations, or a related field.
• Strong research, analytical, writing, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex legal or policy issues to non-legal audiences.
• Demonstrated organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and sensitive matters accurately.
• Experience maintaining legislative, regulatory, stakeholder, compliance, budget, or project trackers with a high degree of accuracy.
• Ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism.

Preferred Skills/Education

• Experience working in government affairs, corporate affairs, public policy, or political environment (Capitol Hill, state house, trade association, consultancy, or corporate office).
• Familiarity with budget tracking and operational support systems (e.g., procurement platforms, expense tools).
• Demonstrated ability to work effectively with senior executives and external partners. Preferred Qualifications

• Experience working in government affairs, corporate affairs, public policy, or political environment (Capitol Hill, state house, trade association, consultancy, or corporate office).
• Familiarity with budget tracking and operational support systems (e.g., procurement platforms, expense tools).
• Demonstrated ability to work effectively with senior executives and external partners.

About this role:

Wells Fargo is seeking a Registered Client Associate in Wealth and Investment Management as part of Wells Fargo Advisors.  Learn more about the career areas and business divisions at wellsfargojobs.com.

In this role, you will:

• Assist Financial Advisor(s) with sales, service and operational related activities such as providing service to clients via telephone, direct interaction and/or written correspondence
• Facilitate Financial Advisor and client requests for account related information and/or quotes, scheduling and preparing for appointments with new or prospective clients
• Establish and service client accounts, prepare forms, research account inquiries and/or issues
• May also perform various administrative functions for the Financial Advisor(s) and Branch Management including, but not limited to, tracking referrals, coordinating and executing marketing campaigns, establishing and maintaining files to meet the firm's regulatory requirements, and establishing and maintaining filing and record keeping necessary to support efforts to service and grow client relationships
• When applicable, acts as the liaison for all referral sources by reviewing paperwork for completeness and forwarding to management for review

Required Qualifications:

• 1+ year of Brokerage and Client Services support experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education
• US only: Successfully completed Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) Series 7 and 63 examinations (or FINRA recognized equivalents) sufficient to qualify for immediate FINRA registration

Desired Qualifications:

• Brokerage client support experience
• Administrative support experience in financial services
• Experience interacting directly with customers
• Intermediate Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint) skills
• Client service focus with the ability to listen to customer needs and recommend solutions
• Ability to prioritize work, meet deadlines, achieve goals, and work in a dynamic and complex environment

Job Expectations:

• US Only: Obtaining and/or maintaining appropriate FINRA license(s) is required for ongoing employment in this position. Compliance with state law registration and licensing requirements is mandatory. In addition to state registration and licensing requirements, specific product licenses or SAFE licensing may apply. Additional requirements include meeting enhanced financial fitness and criminal background standards. Wells Fargo will initiate the FINRA licensing review process at the time of offer acceptance. For specific FINRA qualification exams obtained after 9/30/2018, the Securities Industry Essentials (SIE) exam co-requisite is required.

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

Finance serves as a strategic partner to a global business portfolio exceeding $18B across the Medical Surgical Portfolio, Americas Region-Led Markets, and Global Commercial Transformation. This team drives financial planning, forecasting, performance management, and executive decision support, helping leaders make informed investment and growth decisions across a complex global organization.
This position is based onsite at Medtronic Operational Headquarters (OHQ) in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Limited travel may be required.

The Financial Consultant serves as the core Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) lead for Portfolio+, providing leadership across forecasting, reporting, performance management, and executive financial deliverables. This role partners with Operating Unit Finance, Strategy, and cross-functional stakeholders to deliver actionable insights, drive alignment, and support portfolio-level business decisions.

Primary Responsibilities

• Lead core FP&A processes across Portfolio+, including forecasting, reporting, financial analysis, and performance management activities.
• Lead the Latest Best Estimate (LBE) process, including consolidation, financial analysis, risk assessment, opportunity identification, and stakeholder alignment.
• Develop and coordinate Monthly Financial Review (MFR), Executive Committee (ExCom), and other executive financial deliverables.
• Analyze financial results, forecasts, and key business drivers to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and performance impacts.
• Manage forecast tie-outs, variance analysis, and reporting accuracy across systems and financial submissions.
• Own the Portfolio+ FP&A calendar, coordinating milestones, deadlines, inputs, reviews, and deliverables across stakeholders.
• Partner with global Operating Unit Finance and Strategy teams to align assumptions, expectations, risks, opportunities, and key financial deliverables.
• Drive process improvements through simplification, standardization, and enhanced financial reporting and analytics.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree with 10+ years of Finance or Accounting experience OR Advanced degree with 8+ years of Finance or Accounting experience.
• Experience in financial planning and analysis, forecasting, budgeting, financial reporting, and performance management.
• Experience developing executive-level financial presentations, reporting, and business insights.
• Experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders to support business decision-making.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Power BI.
• Knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
• Proficiency with Excel, Power BI, Tableau, Worldwide Reporting (WWR), and Global Standard Reporting (GSR).
• Experience translating complex financial data into actionable insights and business recommendations.
• Experience presenting financial results and recommendations to senior leadership within a complex global organization.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

En quête d’une première expérience qui fait la différence ?

Rejoins Airbus Atlantic et donne une trajectoire unique à ton parcours grâce à ce stage.

Nous sommes un leader mondial sur le marché des aérostructures, des sièges pilotes et des fauteuils passagers premium.

Dans le cadre de votre formation initiale, vous recherchez un stage obligatoire ou intégré dans une année de césure, d’une durée de 4 à 6 mois, vous permettant de valider votre année.

Une offre de stage intitulée «STAGE 2027 - Gestion de Projet IA & Innovation Qualité - Structure A350 (H/F) » vient de s'ouvrir au sein d’Airbus Atlantic sur le site de Montoir de Bretagne.

Cette mission débutera en janvier 2027 (date sujette à flexibilité) pour une durée de 6 mois.

Découvrez le site en vidéo :

Retrouvez Airbus Atlantic en vidéo et la Présentation du site de Montoir de Bretagne

Tâches et responsabilités :

Vous rejoindrez une équipe de 30 personnes au sein du département  « Qualité A350 Structure » en charge de la Qualité Produit de l'unité de production A350 Structure

Encadré par votre tuteur, vous interviendrez sur les activités suivantes :

Innovation & Roadmap IA :

• Définir et déployer une roadmap pour intégrer de l'IA au sein des activités qualité opérationnelles (inspections, analyses correctives, analyses préventives)
• Piloter des Proof of Concepts (POC) par métier pour garantir une adoption concrète et efficace des solutions
• Explorer les opportunités liées aux data et la digitalisation
• Supporter le “Tech Bar Qualité IA” dans l'innovation au quotidien

Excellence Opérationnelle & Data

• Optimiser les activités de surveillance via la clusterisation des Non-Conformités
• Augmenter la pertinence des mini audits afin de mieux cibler les risques
• Assurer le lien entre les changement liés à l’IA et la conformité vis à vis de nos référentiels

Culture Qualité & Formation

• Accompagner la montée en compétences de l’équipe qualité sur l’IA au travers d’un tutorat ludique et innovant
• Contribuer à l'amélioration continue du système de management de la qualité
• Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de production et Manufacturing Engineering

Durant votre stage, vous développerez les compétences suivantes en lien avec votre formation :

• Déploiement de solutions Data/IA en milieu industriel : traduction d'un besoin métier complexe en solutions digitales (algorithmes, data analytics)
• Pilotage de projets Innovation & IA : de la construction d'une roadmap stratégique au déploiement de Proof of Concepts (POC) concrets sur le terrain
• Conduite du changement et Leadership : vulgarisation technique, animation d'ateliers et transfert de compétences pour embarquer les équipes
• Management de la Qualité & Excellence Opérationnelle : maîtrise des référentiels aéronautiques et utilisation de l'analyse de données pour optimiser la résolution de problèmes

Parlons de VOUS !

Vous préparez actuellement un diplôme de niveau Bac +4/+5 (ou équivalent) dans le domaine de l'Intelligence Artificielle, de la Data Science, de l'Informatique  ou une discipline apparentée.

Vous avez les connaissances et compétences suivantes :

• Vous êtes passionné par les nouvelles technologies et l'intégration de l'intelligence artificielle (IA).
• Vous avez des notions de conduite du changement.
• Vous disposez d'excellentes capacités d'analyse face à des situations complexes et faites preuve d'esprit de synthèse.
• Savoir être : Curiosité, Esprit d'équipe, Bonne communication, Capacité d'adaptation

Langues:

• Anglais : courant
• Français : courant

Vous pourrez être amené(e) à vous déplacer avec votre tuteur.

Parlons de NOUS !

Rejoindre Airbus Atlantic en tant que stagiaire, c'est :

• Participer à des projets ambitieux, à la pointe de la technologie, visant à construire l’avion de demain tout en répondant aux défis environnementaux,
• Acquérir des compétences dans un environnement dynamique qui encourage la créativité et l'initiative, avec une approche entrepreneuriale,
• Évoluer au sein d'une organisation solidaire, qui valorise la proximité et l'humain.

Notre processus de sélection

Toutes les candidatures seront soigneusement examinées par un recruteur.

Si votre candidature est présélectionnée, vous serez invité à réaliser un entretien vidéo afin de vous présenter.

Après évaluation, les candidats retenus seront contactés pour un entretien avec le manager ou le tuteur qui procédera alors à la sélection finale.

jobs.description:
